clue.text: Tory at liberty to receive Republican fellow member

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: the word for 'at liberty' takes the Republican letter inside it

parts.note: someone at liberty is free

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician, newly freed, welcomes a Republican colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A confrère is a colleague, a fellow member of a profession or society.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase mushrooms: they're in your arms

indicators.note: signals that the word for purchase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to purchase is to buy
ceps are porcini mushrooms

explanation.surface: Someone buys mushrooms and carries them home in their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps are the large muscles at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: Lightly brush a salad ingredient outside

indicators.note: the salad ingredient sits outside, wrapping around the single letter A

parts.note: cress is a common salad leaf

explanation.surface: Instructions to brush a salad leaf gently with dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to touch or stroke gently, lightly brushing against something.

clue.text: Action intended to dispatch a one-time Irish nationalist

parts.note: a legal action is a case

indicators.note: dispatch means get rid of, so the letter A is removed from the word for intended

parts.note: something intended is meant

explanation.surface: A plan to kill an old Irish revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Casement was an Irish nationalist executed by the British in 1916. 'to dispatch' removes A from MEANT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Casement was a leading Irish nationalist hanged for treason in 1916, so he is a historical example.

clue.text: Bearing gun going round island

indicators.note: the gun word encircles the island letter, so it goes round it

parts.note: gat is old slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Carrying a gun around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing in the sense of carriage or way of walking is one's gait.

clue.text: Singer from Maine introducing a play about Jones's partner?

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, which leads in the rest

indicators.note: A plus the word for play goes about, around, the partner of Jones

parts.note: to lark is to play about
Dow and Jones founded the Dow Jones financial index

explanation.surface: A performer from Maine stages a show about a business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dow Jones is the US stock index named after Charles Dow and Edward Jones; 'Singer' is crossword shorthand for a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is an American songbird, and birds are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Female group damaging a number of ships?

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
ill as an adjective can mean harmful or damaging

explanation.surface: A gang of women wrecking things.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet, a group of ships sailing together.

clue.text: European runs out to get anorak

indicators.note: the runs letter goes out, being removed from the European

parts.note: a Greek is a European
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A European dashes outside to fetch a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, not the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, much like a geek.

clue.text: Location a popular film is about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the film and the word is are read backwards

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's popular 1982 film

explanation.surface: A place that a well-known movie is set in.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location where something is situated.

clue.text: Edmund II's son tucking into very hard fish

definitions.note: read as 'Edmund II is', the 's being the verb

indicators.note: the son letter is tucked into the gap between the two words

parts.note: iron is proverbially very hard
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A medieval king's son eats a tough fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund II of England was nicknamed Ironside; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Ironside was the byname of the English king Edmund II, who reigned in 1016.

clue.text: Trendy label worn by a Liberal, having several sides

parts.note: hep is an old word for fashionable
a tag is a label
something worn is on a person

explanation.surface: A fashionable badge pinned on a Liberal politician who has many sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Heptagonal means seven-sided, so it is a particular case of having several sides.

clue.text: The culminating point of months in service?

indicators.note: the months letter sits in the middle of the service word

parts.note: an ace is a winning serve in tennis

explanation.surface: The peak of a long career in the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of achievement.

clue.text: Retired sleuth visiting Alpine ridge and similar things

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole construction is read backwards
the sleuth goes inside the ridge as a visitor

parts.note: an arête is a sharp mountain ridge
tec is short for detective

explanation.surface: A former detective climbs an Alpine ridge, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses the whole construction, not just the sleuth, giving ARETECTE read backwards; an arête is a knife-edge mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera means 'and the rest', standing for other similar things.

clue.text: Dried fruit Ailsa regularly fed to cats and dogs?

indicators.note: the selected letters are fed into the middle of the weather word

parts.note: it is raining cats and dogs, so the phrase suggests rain

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the name gives its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Ailsa routinely feeds dried fruit to her pets.
explanation.walkthrough: The pets are a false trail: 'raining cats and dogs' means heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common dried fruit.

clue.text: Very dry American senator in Rome once

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: A humourless American politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was a Roman senator, one of the assassins of Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Fly east, gripped by endless craving for Indian food

parts.note: a ked is a wingless parasitic fly that lives on sheep

indicators.note: the east letter is held within the shortened craving
the last letter of the craving word is removed

parts.note: greed is a craving

explanation.surface: An insect heads east, overcome by a desire for curry.
explanation.walkthrough: A ked is the sheep ked, a fly, though few solvers know it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, fish and eggs that came to Britain from colonial India.

clue.text: Extremely obvious alias for a Honshu port

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

parts.note: aka means 'also known as', introducing an alias

explanation.surface: A thinly veiled false name for a Japanese harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city on Honshu, the largest Japanese island.

clue.text: London thoroughfare accommodating elder, say, in 14's time

indicators.note: the possessive and time letter give room to the tree, which sits between them

parts.note: the answer at 14 across means a small navy, so a fleet's
the elder is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: A London street housing an older person in naval days.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is the London street long home to British newspapers. 14 is the answer to 14 across, read here as a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet Street is a famous street in the City of London, a thoroughfare.

clue.text: Complete costume for a group of players

definitions.meaning: an outfit of matching garments worn together
a band of musicians or actors performing together

explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is both a coordinated outfit and a group of performers.

clue.text: Old book about reformed con at Lima!

definitions.text: Old book about reformed con at Lima!

indicators.note: the old and book words go about, either side of, the anagram

parts.note: ex means former or old
Mark is a book of the New Testament

indicators.note: reformed means made again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old volume telling how a convict was reformed in Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' makes CLAMATION from CON AT LIMA; the clue ends with the very symbol it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation mark is the punctuation mark the clue itself ends with.

clue.text: Man on board's blunder before work

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A sailor's error before beginning his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a chess piece, so a man on the chessboard.

clue.text: Eccentric running through a university city?

definitions.meaning: an eccentric is an off-centre wheel converting rotary to back-and-forth motion

explanation.definitionFit: A cam is an eccentric engine part, and the Cam is the river of Cambridge.

clue.text: Aquatic bird cooked to welcome new correspondent

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: the cooked word welcomes the new letter inside it

parts.note: fried is a way of cooking

explanation.surface: A swan is roasted to greet a new letter-writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A penfriend is someone you correspond with by letter, often abroad.

clue.text: Member is dynamic over English law-making

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: vital means full of energy, dynamic

explanation.surface: A dynamic figure dominates English lawmakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Legislative describes the making of laws, as a legislature does.

clue.text: City nutcase finally stabs surgeon outside church

indicators.note: the surgeon, already stabbed, wraps round the church letters
the letter stabs into the surgeon's name, going inside it

parts.note: Joseph Lister was a pioneering antiseptic surgeon

indicators.note: takes only the last letter of the word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A madman knifes a doctor outside a church in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stabs' puts E into LISTER, making LEISTER; that goes 'outside' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Captured, like some doves

definitions.meaning: seized or arrested by the police
the ... dove has a dark ring on its neck

explanation.definitionFit: Collared is slang for arrested, and the collared dove is a common species.

clue.text: Initial change for fearsome woman going out

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre, a fearsome woman

explanation.surface: A frightening woman changes her first name before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is the act of going out or leaving a place.

clue.text: Cereal plant, one unknown in West

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress
I is the Roman numeral one
z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A mystery crop grown out West.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is a cereal crop, also called corn.

clue.text: Worry, hearing of sweltering conditions in East London

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than written
East End Cockney speech drops the initial h

parts.note: sweltering weather means heat

explanation.surface: Fretting about a heatwave in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the dialect of London's East End, drops the h sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat at someone is to worry or trouble them, as in 'what's eating you?'.
